## reference · empty-state-and-unavailable-item-ux
* Empty states should not be left blank, as this can cause confusion and decrease user confidence.
* Empty states can be used to communicate system status, increase learnability, and provide direct pathways for key tasks.
* A brief system message within the content area can increase the visibility of system status and user confidence.
* Inaccurate system-status messages for empty states can be harmful and cause users to distrust the application.
* Empty states can provide contextual help, such as "pull revelations", to teach users about features and functionality.
* Empty states should provide direct pathways for getting started with key tasks, such as links to relevant documentation or buttons to create content.
* Empty states can be used to provide explicit instructions on how to complete tasks associated with populating the empty state.
* Examples of effective empty-state design include:
  + Displaying a message stating "There are no records to display for the selected date range"
  + Providing a link to create content, such as a "Create" button
  + Offering contextual help, such as "Star your favorites to list them here"
* Empty states should be intentionally designed, not left as an afterthought, to increase usability, learnability, and discoverability of key features.
Sources: https://www.nngroup.com/articles/empty-state-interface-design/
